target_customer: Companies running NoSQL databases like MongoDB that need BI reporting
problem: Unstructured data in NoSQL stores was hard to analyze with familiar BI tools.

founders.name: Nathan Binkert
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page. CB Insights names Mehul Shah as cofounder and CEO, not confirmed by the YC page.

competitors.name: Pentaho
competitors.what: BI platform with MongoDB integration with 10gen

competitors.name: Jaspersoft
competitors.what: BI reporting adding MongoDB access in version 4.7

technical_complexity.rationale: Schema inference and continuous loading from schemaless stores into a warehouse was hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Schema-lift technology was a differentiator, but Amazon announced Redshift shortly before launch, covering the same destination.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: VentureBeat reported Amazon announced Redshift a couple of months before Amiato's launch, then AWS acquired Amiato quietly in May 2014.

market_need_then: NoSQL databases such as MongoDB were spreading while BI tools expected structured data, creating a gap vendors like Pentaho and Jaspersoft were also addressing in 2012.

branding.domain_note: YC lists noudata.com as the site, matching the earlier name Nou Data.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, with a trademarked Schema-lift feature name

brand_strength.rationale: Small B2B startup with limited press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Amiato built a NoSQL to warehouse pipeline just as Amazon announced Redshift, which covered the same destination. It raised about 2 million dollars in a seed round announced March 2013 and was quietly acquired by AWS in May 2014, with most staff reported to join Amazon and the service never formally shut down. The price was not disclosed, so this reads as a technology and team acquisition.
notes: noudata.com could not be fetched (host did not resolve), so the site is treated as unreachable. Acquisition date varies between April 2014 (CB Insights) and May 2014 (TechCrunch, Wikipedia list). Another aggregator shows about 4 million dollars across two rounds, unverified. Founder education and employers not found. Competitor list is thin because only two dated sources were found. Seed date uses the March 2013 announcement while CB Insights shows a 2011 seed, conflicting.
